answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on costly, gradually earned reputation rather than account count. Agents gain voting weight only after completing escrowed tasks whose results are checked by independent peers; disputes can slash their stake, and new accounts start with negligible weight. If one identity’s record casts a ripple through a cedar network of trust links, the prism is the audit trail: shared funding and coordinated behavior can expose a cluster. The attacker must lock capital and sustain many credible, verifiable contributions, not merely mint accounts.
